_comment: MATERIAL CORRECTIONS TO FIGURES THIS PLATFORM HAS ALREADY PRINTED.
THE PRACTICE. When a figure the site has been printing changes materially — not because
the world moved, which is what a dated as-of line already says, but because what we held
was wrong or incomplete — the change carries a dated note WHERE THE FIGURE IS PRINTED,
saying what it was, what it is now, and why it moved. The note is data rather than a
sentence in a commit message, because a commit message is read by whoever is looking for
it and a reader of the page is not.
WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH TO JUST FIX THE NUMBER. A reader who saw €421 million in cement last
month and sees €655 million today has no way, from the page, to tell a correction from a
new award — and those are different facts about how much this platform knew. Silently
restating a figure asks to be trusted on the new one while hiding that the old one was
shipped. The note is the cost of having printed it.
WHAT COUNTS AS MATERIAL. A figure a page states in its own prose, moved by enough that a
reader who acted on the old one would act differently. A rounding change is not one. A
figure that has never been rendered is not one either: it was never printed, so there is
nothing to correct in front of anybody.
THE FIELDS.
figure   WHICH printed figure, from the closed list in sources/sector_map.py. Closed
because a note pinned to a figure nobody renders is a note nobody reads, and
a typo would produce exactly that, silently.
date     when the correction was made, which is what the note prints.
was/now  the figure as it read and as it reads, in the site's own money wording.
what     one sentence a reader can act on.
why      how the platform came to be wrong, in our own words rather than in a passive
one. A correction that will not say whose miss it was is half a correction.
sources  the document that settled it.
AN ENTRY IS NEVER REMOVED. The figure moving again is a second entry, not an edit of the
first: a correction that can be quietly rewritten is not a correction.

corrections.what: Committed money in European cement was corrected upwards by €234 million, a little over half again as much as the figure this page had been stating.
corrections.why: A retro-check of the Commission's own funding registers against the sites already on file found an Innovation Fund grant of €234 million to IFESTOS — TITAN's oxyfuel capture retrofit at Kamari — that this platform carried no funding row for, although the project itself has been on file since the cement dataset landed. The figure was not miscalculated: it was calculated over a set we had left incomplete, and the miss was ours rather than the source's.
